title: Performance QuickView Strip: compact per-route & per-model tiles
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Goal: Design a compact, scan-first ‘QuickView Strip’ of micro-tiles that live in the Model and Route lists and surface the most actionable performance signals (latency distribution, throughput, token flow, and incremental cost) with one-line access to drill into the full route/model canvas. The strip must be legible at 280–420px row heights, persist SLO indicators at glance, and support keyboard navigation and screen-reader labels. This ticket covers content hierarchy, micro-chart specs, interaction patterns (hover details, expand-to-canvas, time-range persistence), accessibility contrast decisions, and handoff artifacts (Figma frames + chart spec sheet).

Context and constraints: Redwood Console pages are dense; users want fast diagnostics without opening the full route page. Existing route pages already have full stripe dashboards; the QuickView is intended for triage and surface-level comparisons across dozens of routes/models. We prioritize information density and clear anomaly signals over exhaustive metrics. Keep visual language consistent with console tokens (color token names: critical-red, warn-amber, neutral-ink, cost-green).

Deliverables: 1) Figma frames for Compact Row (collapsed) and Expanded QuickPeek modal; 2) Chart-spec document with rendering guidance for the frontend runtime (SVG/canvas recommendations, target frame-rates, recommended downsampling); 3) Interaction spec for keyboard + touch; 4) Accessibility checklist and contrast tokens; 5) Implementation notes for telemetry team: required pre-aggregations and tag dimensions.

Links: Figma proto (working): https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/quickview-strip, Confluence spec template: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/console/QuickView-Strip-Spec, Prototype video: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/EXAMPLE-QUICKVIEW-VIDEO
acceptance_criteria: Compact QuickView fits within a single row height in Model and Route lists and maintains visual clarity at 90% zoom
Latency microview shows p50 and p95 markers and highlights p99 anomalies with a red band when beyond configured SLO
Throughput micro-sparkline supports 1m/5m/1h aggregation granularity and mouse/touch hover shows exact datapoint + timestamp
Token flow microbar shows request token vs response token averages and a 7d trend delta badge (+/- percent)
Cost micro-tile shows estimated cost per 1k tokens with hover breakdown (model cost, infra cost) using precomputed per-route cost fields
Keyboard users can focus each micro-tile and press Enter to open Expanded QuickPeek; screen readers read succinct alt text for each metric
Design handoff includes chart CSS variables, color tokens, and a small JSON-serializable chart-spec for frontend implementation
design_notes: Row layout: left -> route name (flex 1) -> QuickView Strip (fixed 420px) -> actions

Latency chart: compact stacked area with two thin lines (p50 solid, p95 dashed). p99 rendered as small vertical tick with red outline when > SLO. Y-axis hidden in compact view, visible in expanded modal.
Throughput chart: 32px x 80px sparkline, filled baseline to zero, smoothing=EMA(α=0.25). Tooltip shows raw RPS and bucket timestamp.
Token microbar: 3-segment horizontal mini-bar: prompt tokens / generated tokens / cached tokens. Each segment width = avg proportion. Legend collapsed; color-coded chips visible on hover.
Cost tile: single numeric with small caret delta; on hover show waterfall of allocation (model compute, GPU-hours, caching savings). Currency format USD with per-1k token normalization.
Aggregation guidance: frontend must accept pre-aggregated timeseries at 1m, 5m, 1h windows. When only raw events available, recommend server-side rolling window aggregations before rendering.
Rendering guidance: use canvas for sparkline at >200 rows; use SVG for single-row interactive ticks. Target 60 FPS for hover animations at typical console load.
Anomaly visual treatment: use a 2px red outline + 8% alpha fill for anomaly bands. Avoid heavy drop shadows to keep rows crisp.
Accessibility: color contrast >=4.5:1 for primary text; provide patterned hatch option for users who disable color; alt text examples included in handoff doc.

release_notes_blurb: Adds a compact Performance QuickView Strip to Model/Route lists: surfaces p50/p95 latency, throughput sparkline, token composition, and cost delta for fast triage. Expanded QuickPeek opens full route canvas.
